findings.reason: Confirmed. I read the published text (Forum Math. Pi 10 (2022) e24, Cambridge open-access PDF downloaded 2026-10-01; its per-download stamp changes the byte hash) at pp. 46–47. The formal family is defined on G′ = G_{(n−1)m} with P′ = L′U′, L′ ≅ G_{n−1}^m, by W^0_Ze(ulk; x) = Ψ^{−1}(u) δ_{P′}^{1/2}(l) ∏ W^0(l_i; x_i), and the paper itself notes 'Ψ(u) = 1 for u ∈ U′'. Lemma 8.10 then asserts that the Hecke eigenspace in Ind_{N′}^{G′}(Ψ)^{K′} is spanned by the W^0_Ze(x) over the parameter assignments x, as multisets. For n = m = 2: G′ = GL_2, L′ is the diagonal torus, N′ = U′, and Ψ is trivial on N′. So the space is that of N′-invariant, right-K′-invariant functions, determined by their values F(a,b) on diag(ϖ^a, ϖ^b) for all integers a, b, with no Whittaker support condition. Here W^0_Ze(x1,x2)(diag(ϖ^a,ϖ^b)) = q^{−(a−b)/2} x1^a x2^b. The double coset K′diag(ϖ,1)K′ has q+1 right cosets, and with Ψ trivial they give Tf(a,b) = q f(a+1,b) + f(a,b+1). At x1 = x2 = x, I checked symbolically that F = q^{−(a−b)/2}x^{a+b} and H = (a−b)F both satisfy TF = 2√q x F and TH = 2√q x H, and that the centre acts on both by x². The spherical Hecke algebra C[T_1, T_2^{±1}] therefore has the same eigencharacter on H as on F. Since H(1) = 0 and H(diag(ϖ,1)) = q^{−1/2}x ≠ 0, H is a nonzero eigenfunction independent of F. The only assignment is x = (x,x), so the claimed span is one-dimensional while the eigenspace has dimension at least 2, and Lemma 8.10 is false at coincident parameters. H is the t-derivative at 0 of the family at (xe^t, xe^{−t}). The accepted review's rejection used the generic GL_2 Whittaker function, whose nontrivial character imposes the support condition w_{−1} = 0 and makes the Schur family even in t. That function is not the one defined on p. 47 in this case, so both of its arguments fail. The printed proof's dimension bound counts the Geometric Lemma terms with multiplicity (two here: the Jacquet module of a GL_2 principal series is 2-dimensional), but the spanning set is indexed by distinct assignments. The finding's fix is right: restore E3 as a confirmed error affecting a stated result, correct the extraction's verification, its embedded review and the original review's E3 record, and keep /spherical-collision, the corrected /spherical-span, G4 and the open all-parameter repair. E13's withdrawn clause referring to the flawed Lemma 8.10 should be restored with this precise scope. The counterexample shows only that the spanning claim fails at collisions; it does not show a failure of the direct-integral argument in general, or of the main newform theorem. arXiv 2110.09070v4 (SHA-256 32326ab8…83a6c, re-fetched) is still the latest version, with the same lemma.
